title: One Installation Job per Factory Order — Installation Jobs Operations Manual
content:
**Rule.** A customer holds one **Installation Jobs** record for every factory order delivered to the branch, so the number of installation jobs a customer may hold is not capped by itself. A factory order that already has an installation job that is not cancelled never gets a second one. Units remade after delivery are installed on the same job.

An installation job is opened when the factory order arrives at the branch; each job carries its own job number, the factory order whose units it installs, the window contract or door contract it installs, its installation method, the date it was opened, the openings or door units to install, and whether the job is permitted and inspected.

## What decides whether a second job may exist

The test is made on the system record of the factory order's existing jobs, not on what the customer says. It looks at the jobs already recorded for that same factory order and at their status:

| Existing job for the same factory order | Can another installation job be opened for that factory order? |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| One that is opened, scheduled, in progress, completed or closed | No |
| Only cancelled jobs | Not barred by this test — a cancelled job does not count toward it |

The test is per factory order. A different factory order of the same customer is a separate object and has its own job.

## Points of the rule

- **No customer cap.** The company sets no maximum number of installation jobs per customer; a customer with several delivered factory orders holds as many jobs as there are such orders.
- **Remakes.** A unit remade after delivery does not open a new job; it is installed on the job that already carries its factory order.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A customer with two factory orders delivered to the branch, one for a window contract and one for a door contract, holds two installation jobs, one for each order.
- For a factory order whose only job is cancelled, this test does not bar another job; a factory order whose job is completed never gets a second one.
